book_beyond_the_door.title: Beyond the Door
book_beyond_the_door.author: Usher
pages: This is a story about an old mansion at the top of the village.

Who owns that mansion?
It had been empty for far too long.
No one had ever opened its door. The hinges were rusted with age, and the handle was thick with cobwebs.

Some said there was treasure beyond it.
Along with a monster guarding it.
Could the rumors be true? If so, they were worth verifying. I devoted my whole life to finding the key.
With a trembling heart, I finally opened the door.

But
behind it
was
another door.

"There's only one key!"
I howled in anguish.
Fortunately, though, the inner door wasn't locked.
With a shaking hand, I turned the knob. A monster? Or treasure?

Creeeak--
The door opened.
It was outside.

book_perfect_alibi.title: The Perfect Alibi
book_perfect_alibi.author: Usher
pages: It wasn't me who committed the murder that night.
I have a perfect alibi.

I held my head high and shouted proudly.
"I was asleep at that hour!"

"Who were you sleeping with?"
the detective asked.
There were no witnesses.
Thinking it over again, it's not a perfect alibi.

book_life_as_a_cat.title: How to Live as a Cat
book_life_as_a_cat.author: Usher
pages: Living as a human is exhausting!
So I decided to become a cat.

In the morning I basked in the sun,
and in the afternoon I napped.
Meals were fish.
It was a satisfying day as a cat.
But the next morning, I realized I had to go to the shop and work.
I became human again.

book_culprit_is_here.title: The Culprit Is Among Us
book_culprit_is_here.author: Usher
pages: In 1977, a murder took place at a party in the West.
The host of the party was found cold and dead after drinking poisoned wine.
As it happened, a famous detective was present, and he immediately sealed every door.

"The culprit is in this room."
When he said this, the crowd murmured.
Through deduction, the detective let people out of the room one by one.
When the last person left, the detective said,
"Now there's no one left in here."

book_love_in_three_seconds.title: Falling in Love Takes Only 3 Seconds
book_love_in_three_seconds.author: Usher
pages: The summer I turned 15, I fell in love the moment I first saw her.
Only three seconds were enough.
In the first second, I looked at her face. Her red hair and shining eyes were beautiful.
In the next second, I heard her laugh. Her voice was clear, without a speck of dust.
In the third second, I wondered whether to ask her name.

But I had never spoken with any woman other than my mother.
So I couldn't ask her name.
I still don't know her name.

book_resolve_before_death.title: Resolve Before Death
book_resolve_before_death.author: Usher
pages:
I will die tomorrow.
So I decided to spend my last day meaningfully.
I wrote the letter I'd put off for so long, met a friend I love, and even saw the sea.
By the time I got home, I felt quite good.
So I decided to put off dying.

book_last_summer.title: I Know What You Did Last Summer
book_last_summer.author: Usher
pages: I know what you did last summer.
The man's hands trembled as he read the letter.
He was a shut-in who never left his house, and he had told no one where he'd been.

"How does he know my secret?"
He cautiously turned the letter over.
"Summer-limited cold noodles are back on the menu."
He looked at the sender. It was a flyer from the regular restaurant he often ordered delivery from.
The next day, the man went out for cold noodles.

book_detectives_last_trace.title: The Detective's Last Trace
book_detectives_last_trace.author: Usher
pages:
A locked-room case.
The door was firmly locked from the inside.
The windows were blocked with iron bars.

The victim lay in the middle of the room.
The detective stood there and pondered for a long time.
Then he said,
"I have no idea."
He called the police. That was the detective's final case.

book_unsent_letter.title: The Unsent Letter
book_unsent_letter.author: Usher
pages: Today, too, I write a letter to you.
But I won't send it, will I...
I wrote yesterday, and the day before, faithfully. The feelings I couldn't deliver now number over 300 letters.
Even if I wanted to send them now, stamps cost too much.
I realized that an unsent letter is no different from a diary.
So from now on, I'm going to write a diary.

book_girl_in_the_alley.title: He Was Always Standing in That Alley
book_girl_in_the_alley.author: Usher
pages: Every day at three in the afternoon, a man waited for someone in the same spot.
Rain or snow, he was always there.
One day I couldn't contain my curiosity and asked on impulse.
"What are you waiting for?"
"Four o'clock."
Ah. An hour later, he went home.
